want.who_she_is: Nora Ashby, 27. Licensed home health aide for the county agency out of Rossiter — six houses on a fixed route off County Road 9, two of them her own family. Her father Roy had a stroke eight months ago and his right side never came back; her uncle Ward holds the power of attorney and signs her hours, so she is paid by her father's brother to put her hands on her father. Her apartment is over the laundromat in town; rent is weekly and the agency pays weekly. WHAT SHE HAS TO LOSE: the license and the route, both revocable by one woman. Off the route she is a relative who has to knock.
want.appetite: To be wanted by men who cannot get through a day without her hands on them. It cannot complete — need resets every morning, and every man who starts needing her a notch more than the sheet says pulls it further in. The thing she wants is the moment the needing stops being clinical, and that moment has to happen again tomorrow.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: an assigned route. Two hours a house, daylight only, gloves on, a checklist Cheryl reads back on Friday. She knocks, waits, and leaves when the sheet says. TOP: keys to four houses, her own hours, night visits nobody scheduled, and the checklist a formality — because by then none of them are calling the agency, they are calling her.
want.charge_note: The reversal: men whose authority over her was total now need her hands to get through a day, and the county pays her by the hour to give them. Each flip is one man asking for something the sheet does not list. The taboo: it is blood AND it is her job, and each fact is the other one's cover — every touch here has a clinical name, which is what makes it deniable, which is what lets it go further.

why_this_person.npc_roy: Roy Ashby, 57. Her father, right side gone since March. He ran everything and decided everything, and now the first hour of his day is her hands on him. Being wanted by him means it was never actually about authority.
why_this_person.npc_dane: Dane, 29. Home on a rebuilt knee, wife gone, nothing to do all day but wait for the visit. He never had power over her, so his wanting is not a reversal — it is the only appetite in the game with nothing to lose, which makes it the fastest ladder and the least deniable.
why_this_person.npc_ward: Ward Ashby, 49. Roy's younger brother, holds the power of attorney. He signs the hours, so every dollar she has passed through the hand of the man who decides how long she is alone in that house. He has never said what he thinks that is worth.
why_this_person.npc_marlon: Marlon Teague, 44. Six weeks out of back surgery, and whatever the player named him. He is the man on the route who shows her what this is when it is only a job — or, named closer, the one who proves it never was.
why_this_person.npc_cheryl: Cheryl Pike, 50s. Her supervisor. The standard, and the brake — the only person who knows what the job is supposed to be, and the only one who can take the route away.

decisions.note: Premise chosen against the grain of the repo, not with it. Female + blood family is 6 of the 8 existing v2 games, and the corpus says premise is 0 of 30 reasons a game here is loved against freedom at 25.9%. So the differentiation is placed in the three §1 declarations all eight games answered by default: `written` recorded as a choice, a start choice shipped in 0.1 rather than retrofitted, and the kinship picker on two of the men.

The visiting got a job. Bare 'scattered kin' had no engine for the visits; a home health aide route forces the map to be a town (closing the one-house trap structurally), makes the repeatable surface body contact by construction, and answers release 41 mechanically. Cost: the cast skews toward men who are recovering or impaired, which the board phase must keep from reading as infirm.

who_climbs = 'cast' — declared, not defaulted. All five measured v2 games sit at 19-29%, inside a band no shipped game in the field occupies, because the fork was never asked. One player tier only (`route`), gating hours, keys and locations and nothing sexual. WATCH: gate 34 wants >=60% of meter gating on the cast.

The obligation is rent, and that is an engine constraint rather than a design preference. v2.py:16598/16608/16610 hardcode '— Rent Day', 'Rent is $X' and 'Pay $X rent'; only title/scene/greeting are author-set (template_import.py:2696). A truck note or a medical bill would make the engine lie on the page that charges it.

`fuel` declared as a need rather than a flavour so money gates CONTENT and not only prices. It falls per visit, fills at the gas station, costs money, and shuts every location past walking distance — one object wiring economy to map to needs, and a condition on currency rather than a costs block (gate 16).

WANT §3 AMENDED — one willingness word, not a pair per man. The Want gave every man `access` + `willingness`. the-meters.md W6 reversed that on 2026-08-24 and quotes its own old text as what produced off_season's four characters with four vocabularies. Measured over 13 corpus games: median ONE meter per person, 9 of 13 use the same word for everyone, 88% of thresholds shared. Now: `want` on everyone who climbs, `access` as a second meter on Roy and Dane only — the two arcs that carry the game.

WANT §3 AMENDED — the `route` player tier is deleted and folded into npc_cheryl.trust. Declaring an ascent tier while declaring who_climbs = 'cast' fights the scoreboard on two axes: _school_split counts declared-tier gates on the PLAYER side (gates.py:2026) against gate 34's >=60%-cast (gates.py:5734), and lint_meter_ladder measures declared tiers against the 8-17 rung player-ascent comparator (gates.py:2142-2155). Folding it into Cheryl is also better fiction: the route is hers to give, which the Want already said. Nothing is lost — gate 10's direction test walks every player trait whether declared or not (gates.py:4383-4390).

Rungs placed low and uneven, starting at 4-6. Per-character willingness in the field runs a median of 3 rungs (p25 2, p75 6) with the lowest at ~5 (gates.py:2113-2119); the 8-17 figure is a PLAYER-ascent number and does not transfer to a roster game. 15/35/55/75 is the DoL seed's spacing that templates/board.toml taught to all 16 tiers of five games.

FINDING, not fixed here: templates/board.toml ships a [[needs]] table and the importer does not read one. It reads 24 top-level tables (project, settings, time, player, locations, npcs, canvases, quest_cards, sidebar_items, traits, engine, ui, theme, clothing, items, quests, phone, flags, bank, builds, passes, fast_jobs, story_arc, player_portrait) and `needs` is not among them. A key the engine does not consume fails silently — the exact class SKILL.md warns about, sitting in a template, which is copied harder than a reference file. The needs are declared in board.needs[] here and exist in the game as core_traits + trait_decay + the conditions that read them.

fill re-declared from the finished horizon (31,500) to a v0.1 budget (16,000), keeping the anchor ratio. v0.1 is the one release that ships with NO debt, so its declared budget has to be the one it actually delivers. Shipped scale for comparison: the_season 15,500 across 8 with 35 canvases, mrs_vance 13,309 across 14 with 94. The finished figure is kept per-location as `fill_finished` so the anchor keeps being budgeted against it.

fill re-planned a SECOND time, 16,000 -> 10,000, and the reason is a shape fact rather than a word count. Measured across the repo: the_season also fails gate 1 (4,412 delivered against 15,500 declared) and only mrs_vance clears its own budget — 13,684 across FOURTEEN locations, 69 pools, ~978 words per location. This game has ten locations, so ~1,000 each is the density that actually ships, and 16,000 was extrapolated from a figure no v2 game has ever hit. ALSO LOAD-BEARING: a node-routed act loop is a TRIGGERLESS canvas, so it carries no location and its prose counts toward no location's fill — roughly 1,500 words of this game's best writing sits outside the gate's denominator by construction. That is why the anchor read 710 while the bathroom loop was the longest thing in the build. Not back-filled: 10,000 is above the 5,545 delivered at the time of the amendment, and the gap is what the talk screens close.

rossiter's budget raised 100 -> 300 and written up to it. 100 was planned as a bare corridor; the zone screen has to name four blocks of a town and carry the errands, which is a satellite rather than a corridor. Re-planned and then delivered against — not back-filled: it stood at 170 when the number was changed and the prose was written afterwards.

THREE BUILD-BREAKING DEFECTS THE SOURCE GATES COULD NOT SEE, all found by running `package_from_toml`. (1) `targetType = "canvas"` is not a valid choice target — the importer takes trigger|location|node only (template_import.py:4667); the house form is a cross-canvas node reference, `nodeId = "<canvas>.<node>"`. (2) `exit_block.type = "choice"` is invalid; the set is choices|game_end|location|canvas|trigger. (3) VALID_CLOTHING_SLOTS is a hardcoded seven and `outfit` is not among them. Every one of these was green on all 46 gates. The build is a separate instrument from the scoreboard and neither substitutes for the other.

`npc` is a TRIGGER field, not a canvas field. Ten hubs carried it at canvas level, where the importer drops it — so every portrait hub in the game rendered no portrait, and gate `every hub is met first` reported n/a rather than failing. An n/a is not a pass, and this is what was hiding behind one.

A HUB CHOICE'S `costs` DOES NOT BRAKE IT for gate 26. gates.py:2791 — for a canvas the player walks into rather than routes into by nodeId, _is_free consults the TRIGGER only, so the doctrine's own advice ('price the hub choice') does not satisfy this branch. The brake has to be a day cap on the choice. A trigger-level cap would have taken the character's portrait off the screen for the rest of the day, so every hub rung is day-capped on a flag cleared in [engine.daily_tick] instead.

The playtest harness's 'guidance page resolves cards — 5 of 10 at turn one' is the HARNESS, not the game: check 5 plays every canvas, which fires all five meetings and sets their flags before check 7 counts cards. Verified against the engine's own evaluator (v2.py:15538-15542), which reads flags correctly. Recorded so nobody re-diagnoses it as an F8 leak.

map.shape: County Road 9 runs out of Rossiter past three houses on her route — her father's, her brother's trailer, and the last house twelve miles further on. The town holds the agency that assigns the route, a diner, a gas station, and her apartment over the laundromat. The road is the ground; everything else hangs off it.

board._fill_note: TWO NUMBERS, deliberately. `fill` is the v0.1 budget — 16,000 across ten, anchor roy_house at 4,500 = 28.1% — and it is what gate 1 checks delivered prose against NOW. `fill_finished` is the 31,500 the world is being budgeted toward, kept because the anchor rule is a RATIO that tightens every time any other room grows: budget the anchor against the finished total, not the current one, or it fails while nothing about it got worse. Both written in round numbers before the prose. All three earlier v2 games back-filled this field from delivered word counts and matched their own plan 8/8 while proving nothing.
